newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes track cash lower - Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes track cash lower - Oct 10.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices followed cash markets 70 cents lower on Thursday, with traders failing to strike fixed deals despite the drop in outright values.
Alaskan deltas were flat at $2.30 less November West Texas Intermediate (WTI), which collapsed in the aftermath of a 3.05-cent decline in November heating oil.
Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude followed the fall in WTI, hitting $21.85/22.15 a barrel, versus $22.55/22.85 on Wednesday.
Traders heard talk of a formula deal between a major producer and refiner Thursday, and 500,000 barrels were sold.
But with the average price of WTI down to $24.30 from $25 a barrel on Thurday, some sellers wondered why buyers held out.
Buyers bid at $2.50 under November WTI but favoured greater discounts because of poor margins. Meanwhile, a major producer kept his offer at $2.10.
Line 63 diffs remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
Kern River, from California's San Joaquin Valley, held at $17.20/17.40 a barrel, after rising with postings on October 8.
Prices for Long Beach-based Wilmington crude also remained stagnant at $18.60/18.70 a barrel.
